items.title: Joe Lyde Interview, 1959-05-18
items.q: he was, of course, there was the same thing, Smiley and all were kind of high-class people... The tromboneist's name was Jimmy Compton.

ctx.x: Uh-huh. Uh-huh. Uh, about the jazz in Ireland, do they have the same sort of set up that I read about and hear about in England, you know, little clubs where they, uh...

Well, not... You know what I mean? Yeah. Not... Not when I left. It wasn't as impressive as it was in London. One or two jobs, one or two little bands. The... At the time when I was in high school, and I left high school in 51, uh, they only had, to my knowledge, they only had, uh, Ken Smiley's band. And he left around that time and it was taken over by the trombone player, very good trombone player, called Jimmy Compton, and, uh, he was, uh, he's kept the band going and it's still playing now, to my knowledge. I…
Nothing dirty? Did they play any dirty type music?
